title: Alike
abstract: In Alike (2015), the contrast between a uniform city and a musician’s vivid space allows color to function as narrative information. Repetition links the father’s working life to his son’s school experience, while a late gesture of recognition interrupts that routine. This reading examines color, staging, editing, sound, and animated performance, placing the film in conversation with research on autonomy and creativity without mistaking fictional allegory for empirical evidence.
image_captions: Paste responds to the gray city while commuters walk past him
The colored tree interrupts the uniform city
The father and son are framed by school and work materials
Rows of identical desks make repetition visible
Copi and Paste reconnect beneath the red tree
